sections.title: Letters and combinations
sections.content: Some Hungarian consonants are written with two letters. sz sounds like English s ("see"), while s alone sounds like English sh ("ship") — almost the opposite of what it looks like. zs sounds like the s in "measure", and cs sounds like English ch ("church"). gy, ny and ty are all "wet"-sounding versions of d, n and t — press the middle of your tongue against the roof of your mouth, close to the d in "duke", the n in "canyon", the t in "tune". ly is a spelling leftover: today it's pronounced exactly like y.

One more habit worth building early: Hungarian always stresses the first syllable of a word. Unlike English, where stress hides — is it CONtent or conTENT? — Hungarian never makes you guess. Say every word like you're hitting a drum on beat one, and you'll already sound more confident than most learners.
